scenarios.title: The Teammate's Celebration
scenarios.text: The locker room has a social scene: card games, a weekly dinner, a group that goes out after home games. You have to decide how far into it you want to go.

choices.label: Go all in, within reason
choices.result: You join the card game and the weekly dinner, and skip the late nights. By midseason, you're part of the room.

choices.label: Pick one thing
choices.result: You pick the weekly dinner and nothing else. You know a few teammates well instead of all of them a little.

choices.label: Stay out of it
choices.result: You keep to yourself and your routine. Your kicking is sharp, and nobody invites you anywhere by October.

scenarios.title: The Position Meeting
scenarios.text: Your place on the depth chart comes up in a meeting you weren't invited to, and the long snapper tells you about it at lunch.

choices.label: Ask {coach} directly
choices.result: You ask {coach} where you stand. It's an honest answer: safe, for now, if the next month looks like the last one.

choices.label: Kick and say nothing
choices.result: You say nothing and kick the best week of practice you've had.

choices.label: Call your agent
choices.result: You call your agent, who calls the general manager, who calls {coach}. Everyone knows you asked.

scenarios.title: The New Playbook
scenarios.text: A new coaching staff installs a new playbook and new expectations for the specialists, and the first test is Friday.

choices.label: Learn it cold
choices.result: You learn the new special teams playbook cold, including the parts that aren't yours.

choices.label: Learn your part
choices.result: You learn your part perfectly and nothing else. It's enough.

choices.label: Study with the unit
choices.result: You set up a study session with the snapper and the holder. It turns into a unit dinner.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Comparison
scenarios.text: The media compare you with another young kicker, every week, by name.

choices.label: Call the other kicker
choices.result: You call the other kicker and laugh about it. You agree not to read anything with both your names in it.

choices.label: Use it
choices.result: You put the comparison on your locker and kick every practice like it's a contest.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.result: You stop reading the coverage. It's quieter, and it takes discipline.

scenarios.title: The Charity Donation
scenarios.text: Your aunt asks you to donate to a cause back home: a new roof for the church you grew up in.

choices.label: Give generously
choices.result: You give more than she asked. The church puts your name on a plaque you'll be embarrassed by forever.

choices.label: Give what you planned
choices.result: You give the amount in your budget and explain why. She's a little disappointed and grateful anyway.

choices.label: Run a fundraiser instead
choices.result: You host a fundraiser in your hometown and raise twice the money, with your time instead of your account.

scenarios.title: The Teammate's Advice
scenarios.text: A veteran explains, very calmly, how fast a career can end: his roommate from his rookie year lasted one season.

choices.label: Ask what he did differently
choices.result: You ask what he did differently. His answer has nothing to do with kicking: he saved, he slept, he showed up.

choices.label: Let it scare you
choices.result: It scares you, and you start saving half of every check and sleeping nine hours a night.

choices.label: Shrug it off
choices.result: You shrug and say it won't happen to you. The veteran nods slowly, like he's heard it before.

scenarios.title: The Agent's Warning
scenarios.text: Your agent warns you to be careful about where you're seen: a teammate's photo outside a club just cost him a sponsor.

choices.label: Change your routine
choices.result: You stop going out after home games. You're bored some nights, and safe all of them.

choices.label: Ask what's actually off-limits
choices.result: You ask your agent for a specific list. It's shorter than you feared.

choices.label: Ignore the warning
choices.result: You say you're not doing anything wrong and keep your routine. Your agent sighs.

scenarios.title: The Apartment Neighbor
scenarios.text: Your neighbor works nights and practices drums at noon, the only hour you have for a nap.

choices.label: Knock and talk
choices.result: You knock and explain your schedule. He's a fan, it turns out, and moves practice to the evening.

choices.label: Complain to the building
choices.result: You complain to the building manager. The drumming stops, and so does the neighbor's wave in the hallway.

choices.label: Buy earplugs
choices.result: You buy good earplugs and nap anyway. It works, mostly, and the neighbor waves at you every morning.

scenarios.title: The Unexpected Criticism
scenarios.text: Fans tear into you online after one week of bad practice clips somebody posted.

choices.label: Log off
choices.result: You delete the apps for a week. It's quiet and it helps.

choices.label: Reply with humor
choices.result: You reply with a joke about your own form. It's the most-liked reply of the week, and the tone changes.

choices.label: Let it fuel you
choices.result: You screenshot the worst one and put it on your locker.

scenarios.title: The Second Contract Conversation
scenarios.text: Your agent starts talking about what your next contract could look like, if you last.

choices.label: Ask what lasting looks like
choices.result: You ask what the club looks for in a second contract. The list is specific, and you can work on it.

choices.label: Dream a little
choices.result: You let yourself dream about the house, the car and the security. It's motivating, mostly.

choices.label: Change the subject
choices.result: You say you're not thinking past this season. Your agent says that's the right answer.

scenarios.title: The Veteran's Rules
scenarios.text: The veterans post the locker room's unwritten rules on a whiteboard, and one of them is about you: 'Kickers don't talk in team meetings.'

choices.label: Laugh and follow it
choices.result: You laugh and keep quiet in team meetings. The veterans are disappointed you didn't fight it.

choices.label: Break the rule once
choices.result: You speak once, in a meeting, about something that matters. The room is silent, then a captain nods.

choices.label: Erase it
choices.result: You erase your rule from the whiteboard. It's back the next morning, in bigger letters.

scenarios.title: The Playbook Test
scenarios.text: The special teams coordinator quizzes the rookies on the playbook, out loud, at seven in the morning.

choices.label: Know it cold
choices.result: You've studied, and you answer every question. The coordinator moves on to the next rookie quickly.

choices.label: Bluff
choices.result: You bluff through two answers. The coordinator knows, and assigns you a page of the playbook to copy by hand.

choices.label: Admit you don't know
choices.result: You say you don't know one answer and ask for the right one. The coordinator respects it.

scenarios.title: Learning the Snap Count
scenarios.text: The long snapper's rhythm is different from anything in college, and practice is tomorrow.

choices.label: Ask for extra snaps
choices.result: You ask the snapper for fifty extra snaps after practice. By the end, you can hear the rhythm.

choices.label: Adjust your timing alone
choices.result: You adjust your approach yourself, counting in your head all evening.

choices.label: Ask the snapper to adjust
choices.result: You ask the snapper to speed up for you. He laughs and says no. Then he does it anyway.
